Truthfully? It's probably not what you want to hear, but this is what I would tell myself at your age if I had a time machine:

1) Realize that you're already in a relationship. If you are unsatisfied, you need to leave it and figure out what you want before you start pursuing again.

2) Realize that she's already in a relationship. If she's satisfied enough to be in it willingly, but would drop it to switch up to you, she's not loyal and will not satisfy you long-term.

3) Stop thinking a woman is going to make you happy. That's your job. Get your life together, be complete in who you are, then find a woman who is willing and capable of building the future you'd want together, and commit. Otherwise, you'll always be disappointed, and you'll always be clinging on to an unsatisfying relationship while looking for a better one.

4) Stop obsessing over women you don't know well in a personal manner. That near-perfect woman who would be perfect in a relationship with you, if only you could get a date with her? Somebody, somewhere is sick of her shit right now. If you haven't dated her for a while, your idea of who she is romantically exists only in your head. You have no idea who she is in a relationship. You've got to date her a while before you know if she's worth serious emotional investment. Even if she's really cool in other contexts.

5) Unless you are exceptionally lucky or skilled, most of your relationships will end fairly unpleasantly. Mixing romantic relationships too heavily with your other social/professional circles - such as coworker (and especially subordinates or bosses) - can easily screw up those circles. It's a bad choice unless you're fairly certain it will work well. Back in my day, you could at least have casual sex with coworkers if you could manage the feelings well... but we live in the #MeToo era, so I don't know if even that is a good idea.

5) The dick, hormones, and a need for emotional validation are powerful motivators, especially at your age, so there's a good chance you won't take all this advice seriously. If that is the case, just be honest and open with her. You can play all the pick-up games and try to manipulate the situation to your benefit, but it's honestly not worth the effort. If you spend time with a girl, and she's given you reason to like her, just straight up tell her and ask her on a date. And be okay with the fact that you'll get rejected sometimes. Be genuinely okay with it. There's a million other women out there who you can enjoy and connect with just as well.

6) Regardless of what happens, pay attention and learn from your mistakes.
